title: Claude-assisted discovery of an Apache ActiveMQ Classic code-injection flaw
summary: Horizon3.ai reports a remote code execution flaw in ActiveMQ Classic, introduced about 13 years earlier, that chains the Jolokia management API with network-connector VM transports. Apache rates it important and fixes it in 5.19.4 and 6.2.3.
ai_role: The finder, Naveen Sunkavally, says Claude did a first-pass source analysis and traced the exploit path, and describes the work as 80% Claude with human prompting, a test target and reporting. Apache credits him as finder.
classification_note: The cited sources establish an AI-assisted finding and a coordinated report to Apache on 22 March 2026. They do not establish a zero-day incident; exploitation reports are not assessed here.
remediation_note: Apache's announcement lists 5.19.4 and 6.2.3 as fixed releases; the Horizon3 post cites later releases in its timeline, so check the vendor for the current fixed version. Deployed patch status is not checked.

title: Claude finds a FreeBSD RPCSEC_GSS kernel stack overflow
summary: FreeBSD advisory SA-26:08 describes a stack overflow in the RPCSEC_GSS code that can allow remote code execution in the kernel, with no workaround, affecting all supported versions. It credits Nicholas Carlini using Claude, Anthropic.
ai_role: The advisory credits Claude. Anthropic's report says Claude Mythos Preview found the bug and wrote a working exploit with no human involvement after the initial request; that autonomy claim is Anthropic's own and the advisory does not name the model.
classification_note: The advisory establishes the AI-credited finding and fixes. Neither source establishes that the flaw was exploited in the wild, and the autonomy claim is not independently verified.
remediation_note: The advisory lists corrected releases dated 26 March 2026, including 15.0-RELEASE-p5, 14.4-RELEASE-p1, 14.3-RELEASE-p10 and 13.5-RELEASE-p11. Deployed patch status is not checked.

title: Claude-assisted discovery of a Firefox WebAssembly JIT flaw
summary: Mozilla disclosed a WebAssembly JIT miscompilation vulnerability and credited researchers using Claude. Its advisory rates the impact high and lists Firefox 148 as the fixed release. This record covers one CVE, not the total findings in the Mozilla collaboration.
ai_role: Mozilla explicitly credits Claude-assisted researchers. Anthropic describes human validation and coordinated reporting in the wider collaboration.
classification_note: The cited advisory establishes an AI-assisted vulnerability finding. It does not establish exploitation in the wild or a zero-day incident.
remediation_note: Mozilla lists Firefox 148 as fixing the issue in its 24 February 2026 advisory.

title: Hacktron's AI agent finds a BeyondTrust remote-support command injection
product: BeyondTrust Remote Support and Privileged Remote Access
summary: Hacktron reports an OS command injection in BeyondTrust Remote Support and Privileged Remote Access, rated critical with a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.9 and a variant of CVE-2024-12356 on the same WebSocket endpoint. BeyondTrust published advisory BT26-02 on 6 February 2026.
ai_role: Hacktron says its agents found the flaw through AI-enabled variant analysis during autonomous scans; the post does not detail the human review beyond the team's validation and disclosure.
classification_note: Hacktron's timeline shows a report on 31 January 2026 and a patch before public disclosure. The sources do not establish that the flaw was unknown to attackers beforehand.
remediation_note: Hacktron reports patches for cloud and on-premises deployments (Remote Support 25.3.2 and later; Privileged Remote Access 25.1.1 and later). The BeyondTrust advisory page returned HTTP 403 and was not read; deployed patch status is not checked.

title: Big Sleep identifies an undisclosed SQLite vulnerability
organization: Google Project Zero, Google DeepMind and Google Threat Intelligence
summary: Google reports that Big Sleep, guided by threat intelligence, identified CVE-2025-6965 while the flaw was known to threat actors and at risk of exploitation. Google says its intervention prevented the anticipated use; this is not evidence of an observed successful hack.
ai_role: An AI agent combined code analysis with indicators supplied by human threat-intelligence researchers.
classification_note: Google describes a flaw known only to threat actors before its intervention. This is attributed zero-day context, not an independent finding of active exploitation.
remediation_note: SQLite records a fix on 27 June 2025 and lists release 3.50.2, dated 28 June 2025. The later Google post describes the AI contribution, not the patch date.

title: o3 helps find a Linux kernel ksmbd use-after-free
summary: Independent researcher Sean Heelan reports a use-after-free of sess->user in the ksmbd session-logoff handler, reachable when a second connection binds to the same session. The fix removes the free in smb2pdu.c and is tagged for stable backporting.
ai_role: Heelan ran o3 through the API 100 times on about 12k lines of SMB handler code, with no scaffolding or tools. o3 reported the bug in some runs with a signal-to-noise ratio he puts near 1:50, and he identified the real finding himself and wrote the patch.
classification_note: Per the author's account the bug was not previously known to him; the source does not independently show it was unknown to others.
remediation_note: The kernel commit 2fc9feff45d9 (ksmbd: fix use-after-free in session logoff) authored by Heelan removes the faulty free. The kernel release containing it was not established here.

title: Big Sleep finds a SQLite memory-safety bug before release
organization: Google Project Zero and Google DeepMind
summary: The team reports an AI-agent finding in development code that maintainers corrected on the reporting day. Project Zero states that the defect never reached an official SQLite release, so released users were not affected.
ai_role: Big Sleep performed variant analysis with a starting point selected by researchers. Human researchers verified and reported the finding.
classification_note: Previously unknown does not automatically mean an exploited production zero-day. This case was fixed before an official release; no CVE is asserted here.
remediation_note: Project Zero reports a same-day upstream correction in early October 2024, before an official release; this record does not invent a precise reporting day.

title: AI-generated fuzzing reveals an OpenSSL memory-access flaw
organization: Google Open Source Security Team and OpenSSL
summary: An AI-generated fuzz target revealed an issue in low-level elliptic-curve handling. OpenSSL rates it low severity because vulnerable application use is considered unlikely and the problematic inputs do not arise in ordinary X.509 certificate processing.
ai_role: Google attributes the finding to LLM-generated fuzz targets; OpenSSL credits Google OSS-Fuzz-Gen for the report.
classification_note: The sources document an AI-assisted discovery and public advisory. They do not establish a zero-day exploitation incident.
remediation_note: The 16 October advisory lists corrective commits and planned branch releases; it explicitly did not issue immediate new releases because severity was low. Patch availability is not the same as deployment to users.
